methods.notes: Advertised name is exactly "Atomic" + a 5-character unit ID ("AtomicNNNNN"; the app requires name length >= 6, takes the first 6 characters as the literal "Atomic" and the trailing substring — exactly 5 chars, "00000" if empty — as the unit ID).

device.name: Astral Hoops Atomic V (AF Series)
device.notes:
Programmable LED flow props (hula hoops, wands, fans) sold by Astral Hoops, driven by the "Astral" app (Android package com.astral.astral, v2.0.16 / versionCode 36 analyzed). The app is small, unobfuscated, contains no native libraries, no crypto, no account system and no ad/analytics SDKs; its only network use is fetching public firmware files and a pattern gallery over plain HTTPS. Local-only viability: HIGH — every control function (modes, speed/hue, settings, pattern upload, firmware OTA) runs over the BLE UART with no cloud involvement.
TRANSPORT: Microchip/ISSC Transparent UART BLE module (the well-known public ISSC UUIDs, not vendor-specific). One GATT service 49535343-FE7D-4AE5-8FA9-9FAFD205E455 with TX (phone -> device, write) 49535343-1E4D-4BD9-BA61-23C647249616 and RX (device -> phone, notify) 49535343-8841-43F4-A8D4-ECBE34729BB3. Transparent UART: plain bytes both ways, no BLE-level framing. The app never requests an MTU; in the bulk paths (image upload, OTA) it manually splits payloads into 16-byte GATT writes with ~10 ms between writes. A replacement client should do the same (or negotiate an MTU and confirm the device tolerates it). The app can hold several hoops connected at once and fans each command out to all of them for synchronized control — a group of props is just N GATT connections receiving the same bytes.
WIRE PROTOCOL: ASCII. App -> device commands are short strings beginning with '#'; device -> phone messages are '&'-prefixed status records, simple ACKs ("OK", "BL"), or single control bytes (0x05 ENQ, 0x06 ACK, 0x18 CAN). On connect the app walks a settings query chain #GS -> #GT -> #GD -> #GA -> #GO -> #GE -> #GL -> #GN (sleep seconds, POV stabilization, LED count, battery type, prop type, LED type, battery level, product ID) and the device answers each with the matching '&' record; the device also pushes '&' records spontaneously on state change. See the RX characteristic notes for the full record map.
IMAGERY: custom POV patterns are uploaded as gamma-corrected RGB888 pixel data after a '#D' handshake, in 20-byte chunks each individually ACKed with "OK", and persisted into a numbered pattern slot on the device (see the image_upload_* commands and the features block). Factory patterns can be restored with '#FORMAT'. The vendor hosts a free pattern gallery at https://extras.astralhoops.com/patterns/ (plain HTTPS, pack list via folders.php, per-folder list via patterns.php?folder=<f>, pattern files downloaded as raw bytes).
FIRMWARE / OTA: the MCU is a Microchip/Atmel SAM D21 (ARM Cortex-M0+) — the app's OTA updater reads the Cortex-M0+ CPUID (0x410CC601) and the SAM D21 Device ID register (0x10010305 at its datasheet address 0x41002018) through the bootloader and checks both magic values. The BLE front-end is the matching Microchip ISSC module. Firmware images are PUBLIC, unauthenticated, plain-HTTPS downloads:
  https://astralhoops.com/images/a5.ver      -> dotted version ("5.2.5")
  https://astralhoops.com/images/a5beta.ver  -> beta version ("5.3.0")
  https://astralhoops.com/images/af5.bin     -> raw flash image (~72 KB)
  https://astralhoops.com/images/af5beta.bin -> beta image (~74 KB)
The .bin is a raw image loaded at flash offset 0x2000 (an 8 KB custom bootloader sits at 0x0000-0x1FFF). OTA runs over the same BLE UART: '#B' + 'MCURESET' (device answers "BL") enters the bootloader, which speaks its own ASCII '#' -terminated command language (word/byte/halfword writes staged to RAM and committed per 0x1000-byte flash page, plus an XMODEM-CRC16 block path that appears legacy). See the bootloader_* commands. Treat OTA as MEDIUM confidence overall: the full command sequence is read from the app's updater code, not yet replayed against hardware by this project.
CONFIDENCE: BLE UUIDs, advertised-name filter, command/response inventory, settings chain, image-upload framing, firmware URLs (fetched live; a5.ver returned "5.2.5" and af5.bin downloaded) HIGH from app analysis. MEDIUM: exact '#GV'/'&V' reply layout (both an "&V<string>" branch and a 0x05-led binary triplet branch exist in the parser — needs a live capture), '&M' payload field semantics (mode/group/speed/hue mapping and the mode/item index tables, which live in UI resources), whether "#SS" takes an ASCII or binary operand, whether the XMODEM block path is still exercised, and the gallery folders.php/patterns.php response formats.

credentials.notes: No credentials anywhere: no Wi-Fi, no account, no pairing PIN, no crypto in the app or protocol. Anything in radio range can connect and issue commands; physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: Two app-driven reset levels, both issued over the BLE UART: '#WIPE' clears user customizations (device answers "OK"); '#FORMAT' reformats pattern storage, after which the app re-uploads the factory pattern set. Neither touches the BLE identity or the 5-char unit ID. No credentials or network state exist to clear. A physical/button reset procedure is unknown (not present in the app).

steps.action: Connect and send the wipe_customizations command (#WIPE).
steps.expect: Device replies 'OK'; user customizations are cleared.

steps.action: Connect and send the format_patterns command (#FORMAT), then re-upload pattern images.
steps.expect: Pattern storage is reformatted; factory art must be re-uploaded afterwards (the vendor app re-sends its bundled pattern set).

methods.description: Scan for the "Atomic" name prefix, connect, enable notifications on the RX characteristic, then walk the settings query chain (#GS,#GT,#GD,#GA,#GO,#GE,#GL,#GN) to populate state. No PIN, no bond, no credentials.

steps.action: Power the prop on and scan for an 'AtomicNNNNN' advertisement.
Connect, subscribe to RX notifications, and issue the settings query chain.

setup.notes: No provisioning, no pairing, no account. The prop advertises as soon as it is powered and accepts a connection from any central; the app connects in-app (no OS-level bond). Confidence medium: derived from the app's scanner/connect code, not yet exercised against hardware by this project.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds the prop to a phone or network — switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. The prop handles a single BLE connection at a time, so disconnect (or power-cycle) the old central first; a phone that keeps auto-reconnecting will hold the link.

variants.notes: Hoop/wand/fan share the firmware and protocol; the prop form factor is a device setting (prop/product type index, queried with #GO, set with #SO<i>) rather than a different build. Variant split is by product line, not by protocol.

entities.name: LED Prop
entities.notes: Mode and color control. '&M' records on RX carry current mode/speed/hue. There is no dedicated power on/off command in the observed protocol — props wake on motion/physical switch; the "off" equivalent is the auto-sleep timeout (set_sleep_seconds).

entities.name: Battery Level
entities.notes: '&L<n>' record, n in 0-7 (device-side battery gauge steps; query with get_battery_level). Reported raw — a consumer should scale 0-7 to a percentage or show the step directly.

features.notes:
POV pattern upload (persists on the device into a numbered slot and plays standalone after disconnect). Flow, all over the BLE UART: 1) send image_upload_start ('#D'), wait for "OK"; 2) send a 10-byte header: [width, height, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
   (3 = bytes per pixel, RGB888; width/height each carry a small pad —
   confirm exact padding against a live unit);
3) send the pixel data in 20-byte chunks, waiting for an "OK" after
   EACH chunk before sending the next;
4) after the last chunk send a single byte = the pattern slot number
   to save into, expecting "OK".
Every pixel is passed through a 256-entry gamma/level-correction lookup table before transmission (table hardcoded in the vendor app's pattern designer; functionally a standard LED gamma ramp — recover the exact table from a live capture if bit-exact colors matter). Image geometry equals the prop's LED count (#GD / &D record) by the pattern height. At the GATT layer the app splits all of the above into 16-byte writes with ~10 ms spacing (no MTU negotiation).

Phone-based OTA over the BLE UART into a custom SAM D21 bootloader; firmware images are public unauthenticated HTTPS downloads (https://astralhoops.com/images/a5.ver + af5.bin; beta: a5beta.ver + af5beta.bin). Sequence: compare '#GV' version against a5.ver; download af5.bin (raw flash image for offset 0x2000); send '#B' then 'MCURESET' (expect "BL"), wait ~1 s, send {0x80,0x80,'#'} then 'N#' (expect {10,13}); verify CPUID/DID with the bootloader 'w' read command; erase from 0x2000 ('X00002000#', expect "X\r\n"); program per 4-byte word / 2-byte halfword / 1-byte with W20/O20/H20 commands staged to RAM 0x5000 and committed per 0x1000-byte page with 'Y' commands (each expects "Y\r\n"); finish with the AIRCR SYSRESETREQ write 'WE000ED0C,05FA0004#' and 'MCUDONE'. A 54-byte Thumb helper stub is first written to RAM at 0x20004000 and jumped to — it performs the actual flash writes. An alternate XMODEM-CRC16 block path exists (SOH, block#, ~block#, 128 data bytes, CRC16/XMODEM poly 0x1021 init 0 over the data field; per-block ACK 0x06 / CAN 0x18; a 20-byte variant carries 15 data bytes) but appears legacy — the main updater uses the word-writer. MEDIUM confidence; not yet replayed on hardware.

bootloader_enter.advanced_reason: Firmware update path; an interrupted or malformed flash can brick the prop.
bootloader_enter.description: '#B' followed by 'MCURESET' — enter the SAM D21 firmware-update bootloader; device answers 'BL'. Then follow the OTA sequence in the firmware_update feature notes.

bootloader_erase_app.advanced_reason: Erases the application firmware; the prop is inoperable until a valid image is flashed.
bootloader_erase_app.description: Bootloader: 'X00002000#' — erase application flash from 0x2000 (app region; the 8 KB bootloader below is preserved). Expects 'X\r\n'.

bootloader_mcudone.description: 'MCUDONE' — final OTA handshake token sent after the reset write.

bootloader_mcureset.description: 'MCURESET' (sent right after '#B') — second half of the bootloader-entry handshake; expect 'BL'.

bootloader_read_word.description: Bootloader: 'w<addr6hex>,<count># ' — read memory. Used by the updater to verify the chip: 'wE000ED00,4#' must return {01,C6,0C,41} (Cortex-M0+ CPUID 0x410CC601) and 'w41002018,4#' must return {05,03,01,10} (SAM D21 Device ID 0x10010305). Reply is the raw bytes.

bootloader_reset.description: Bootloader: 'WE000ED0C,05FA0004#' — write AIRCR SYSRESETREQ (system reset), then send 'MCUDONE'. Ends the OTA session and boots the new firmware.

bootloader_write_word.description: Bootloader: 'W20<addr6hex>,<8 hex digits>#' — write one 4-byte word (big-endian hex) at address. Halfword variant 'H20<addr6hex>,<4 hex>#'; byte variant 'O20<addr6hex>,<2 hex>#'. Data is staged to a RAM buffer at 0x5000 and committed per 0x1000-byte page with 'Y20005000,0#' then 'Y00<flashaddr6>,00<len>#'; each 'Y' expects 'Y\r\n'.

format_patterns.description: '#FORMAT' — factory-format pattern storage. Afterwards the factory pattern set must be re-uploaded (the vendor app re-sends its bundled default art through the normal image upload flow).

get_battery_level.description: '#GL' — query battery level; replies '&L<n>' with n in 0-7.

get_mode.description: '#GM' — query current mode; device replies with an '&M' record.

get_version.description: '#GV' — query firmware version. Reply is either an '&V' record (dotted string, e.g. "&V5.2.5") or a 0x05(ENQ)-led binary triplet major.minor.revision — both parse branches exist in the app; confirm on a live unit (MEDIUM).

image_upload_start.description: '#D' — begin pattern image upload; device must answer 'OK' before the 10-byte header and 20-byte ACKed pixel chunks are sent (see the stored_upload feature for the full flow).

pattern_preview_slot.description: '#V' + one selector byte — select/preview stored pattern slot. The selector byte is 46 + slot index (slot 0 = 0x2E '.').

set_battery_type.description: '#SA<i>' — set battery type index; <i> is ASCII decimal.

set_led_count.description: '#SD' + LED count. Firmware >= 5.2 takes the count as TWO raw big-endian bytes appended after the ASCII "#SD"; older firmware takes ONE raw byte. (Operand encoding from the app's settings writer — MEDIUM, confirm against a live unit.)

set_led_type.description: '#SE<i>' — set LED type index; <i> is ASCII decimal.

set_mode.description: '#SM2=<mode>;1=<item>;' — set display mode and menu item within the mode. mode/item are ASCII decimal indices into the device's mode tables (the tables themselves live in app UI resources — index map needs a live capture, MEDIUM). Device replies with an '&M' record.

set_product_id.description: '#SN<text>' — assign the product ID string (ASCII text follows '#SN').

set_prop_type.description: '#SO<i>' — set prop/product type index (hoop/wand/fan); <i> is one ASCII decimal digit/number.

set_sleep_seconds.description: '#SS<n>' — set auto-sleep timeout in seconds; 0 (or ASCII '0') disables. Operand encoding (ASCII vs raw byte) MEDIUM — confirm on a live unit.

set_speed_hue.description: '#SM3=<speed>;4=<hue>;' — set custom animation speed and hue (ASCII decimal operands). This is the primary "pick a color" control for the custom mode.

characteristics.name: TX (phone to device)
characteristics.notes: All commands are ASCII strings written here; string parameters in the templates below are encoded as their ASCII bytes (decimal numbers as ASCII digits). The device answers on the RX characteristic. Writes longer than 20 bytes should be split into 16-byte GATT writes with ~10 ms spacing (the app never negotiates an MTU). The app supports broadcasting every command to multiple connected props for synchronized control. Confidence: command inventory HIGH (every opcode observed in the app); operand encodings for #SS/#SD MEDIUM (see per-command notes).

characteristics.name: RX (device to phone)
characteristics.notes:
Enable notifications via the CCC descriptor after connecting. All device-originated traffic arrives here. Record map (ASCII unless noted):
  '&' (0x26) starts a settings/status record; the second byte
  selects the field:
    &M <mode> <group?> <speed> <hue?>  mode change (>=6 bytes,
      field semantics MEDIUM — mode/group/speed/hue mapping and
      index tables live in app UI resources)
    &L<n>  battery level 0-7
    &S<n>  sleep seconds        &B<n>  brightness
    &T<0|1> POV stabilization   &P<0|1> ISO stabilization
    &C<n>  scan speed           &X<n>  megamix speed
    &D<n> or &D<n,m>  LED count
    &A<n>  battery type         &O<n>  prop type
    &E<n>  LED type             &N<text> product ID string
    &V<text> firmware version (dotted string)
  0x05 (ENQ) as first byte: alternate version response (binary
  major.minor.revision triplet follows — MEDIUM, confirm live).
Simple ACKs: "OK" (image-upload handshake, per-chunk ACK, WIPE, FORMAT), "BL" (bootloader entered), single 0x06 ACK / 0x18 CAN per block on the XMODEM path, and "Y\r\n"-style replies from bootloader commands. '&' records are both replies to '#G*' queries and pushed spontaneously on state change (mode switch, battery).
